children: Shares of Candel Therapeutics fell after the company posted a wider loss from operations and said it's in ongoing dialogue with the Food and Drug Administration about a license application.
Shares dropped 38% to $5.15 in after-hours trading on Thursday. The stock was down 9% through market-close, and is up 49% this year.
The biopharmaceutical company on Thursday posted a third-quarter loss from operations of $23 million or 28 cents a share, compared with a loss of $13.2 million, or 21 cents, the year earlier.
Operating expenses nearly doubled to $23 million from $13.2 million the year before.

Candel said it's still in talks with the FDA about a biologics license application for aglatimagene treatment in prostate cancer. The company  plans to submit the application in the middle of 2027 depending on the result of that dialogue.
